title: How a 9 PM Phone Cutoff Changes What a Godly Man Reaches For
caption:
The last hour of your day is rehearsing the first thought of your next one.

Whatever you reach for right before your eyes close is roughly a rehearsal for who you'll be when they open again. So try one rule: 9 PM, phone goes dark, no exceptions.

At first your hand still reaches for it out of habit. Then it starts reaching for something else instead. The Bible on the nightstand. A notebook and a pen. Real quiet you'd forgotten existed. Actual prayer instead of a scroll.

Paul called this redeeming the time, buying back hours that would otherwise get spent on nothing. "Look carefully then how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, making the best use of the time." Ephesians 5:15-16.

Here's what the cutoff is actually guarding. You're weakest right before sleep, tired and alone with your guard down. That's exactly when the comparison scroll shows up, when lust finds its easiest opening, when the anxious feed becomes the last thing you see before you close your eyes. "Be sober-minded; be watchful." 1 Peter 5:8. Not a detox. A watch.

The last thing you look at is the first thing you fight. Pick tonight. Set the cutoff. See what you reach for instead.
